correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed L_x as a weighted permutation shift with coordinates w_i=a_i x_i. Nonzero a_i make w arbitrary and independent. With all w_i nonzero, first basis vector is cyclic, annihilator t^d-product(w_i) (valid even if inseparable); fixed product has (q-1)^(d-1) solutions. At least one zero decomposes d vertices into Jordan paths; counting cyclic ordered gap compositions with z zero edges gives d(z-1)!/prod m_r! and (q-1)^(d-z) choices. Independent permutation cycles combine as direct sums; colliding module classes merge. Over F7 the idempotent equations u=c v²,v=u² have 4 and 1 solutions for c=1,2; all weighted operator pencils have the same underlying matrix multiset. Fresh independent rank/partition enumeration checked q=2 d<=7, q=3 d<=5, q=5 d<=3, and F7 idempotents; proof covers all prime powers, no separability assumption.

final_claim: For all prime powers q, permutations pi, nonzero structural weights, and x ranging over the algebra, the full Fq[t]-module isomorphism class of L_x has a cycle-factorized distribution: on a d-cycle, invertible cyclic modules Fq[t]/(t^d-c) each occur (q-1)^(d-1) times and each nilpotent partition lambda occurs d(ell(lambda)-1)!/prod(m_r(lambda)!)*(q-1)^(d-ell(lambda)) times. Weighted choices do not change the census, but two F7 two-cycle algebras share this census and are nonisomorphic by idempotent counts 4 versus 1.
limitations: Only one structural permutation with all weights nonzero; characteristically inseparable cyclic modules included; not a classification of arbitrary evolution algebras.
